user.title: Connect an EcoPulse gateway
user.description: Enter the gateway's address on your network and the Home Assistant integration token. You create the token in the EcoPulse web app, on the gateway's Home Assistant settings; it is shown only once.

data_description.host: IP address or host name of the gateway on your LAN.
data_description.port: Port of the gateway's local web server (8080 unless changed). Used without TLS.
data_description.token: Starts with ecp_ha_. This is not the gateway's web password.
data_description.use_tls: Recommended. Required for anything Home Assistant writes to EcoPulse; without it, values can only be read.
data_description.tls_port: Port of the gateway's encrypted Home Assistant API (8443 unless changed; 18443 on a NAS).

zeroconf_confirm.title: EcoPulse gateway found
zeroconf_confirm.description: Found gateway {id} at {host}. Enter its Home Assistant integration token from the EcoPulse web app.

data_description.token: Starts with ecp_ha_. This is not the gateway's web password.
data_description.use_tls: Recommended. Required for anything Home Assistant writes to EcoPulse; without it, values can only be read.
data_description.tls_port: Port of the gateway's encrypted Home Assistant API (8443 unless changed; 18443 on a NAS).

reauth_confirm.title: Token for {name} no longer valid
reauth_confirm.description: The gateway rejected the integration token (usually because it was rotated in the EcoPulse web app), or it presented another certificate than the one Home Assistant trusts. Enter the token.

data_description.token: Starts with ecp_ha_. This is not the gateway's web password.
data_description.use_tls: Recommended. Required for anything Home Assistant writes to EcoPulse; without it, values can only be read.
data_description.tls_port: Port of the gateway's encrypted Home Assistant API (8443 unless changed; 18443 on a NAS).

tls_confirm.title: Confirm the gateway's certificate
tls_confirm.description:
The gateway at {host}:{port} presents a certificate with this SHA-256 fingerprint:

`{fingerprint}`

Open the gateway's Home Assistant settings in the EcoPulse web app and compare it with the fingerprint shown there. Confirm only if both match exactly. Home Assistant will then trust only this certificate. The token has not been sent yet.

data.fingerprint_matches: The fingerprint matches the one in the EcoPulse web app

tls_changed.title: Warning: the gateway presents another certificate
tls_changed.description:
Another device may be answering in place of the gateway at {host}:{port}: it presents a different certificate than the one Home Assistant trusts. Its SHA-256 fingerprint is:

`{fingerprint}`

Open the gateway's Home Assistant settings in the EcoPulse web app. Confirm only if the fingerprint shown there is exactly this one. If it differs, or the web app shows none, do not confirm: cancel and check your network.

data.fingerprint_matches: The fingerprint matches the one in the EcoPulse web app

error.cannot_connect: Cannot reach the gateway. Check the host and port and that the gateway's local web server is enabled.
error.invalid_auth: The gateway rejected the token. Copy it again from the EcoPulse web app or rotate it there.
error.invalid_token_format: This is not an integration token; it must start with ecp_ha_.
error.not_enabled: Home Assistant is not enabled for this gateway, or its firmware is too old. Enable it in the EcoPulse web app and wait for the configuration to reach the gateway.
error.rate_limited: Too many failed attempts from this address. Wait a few minutes and try again.
error.cannot_connect_tls: Cannot open an encrypted connection to the gateway. Check the host and the TLS port, and that the gateway's firmware supports it.
error.certificate_mismatch: The gateway's certificate does not match the confirmed fingerprint. Nothing was sent. Start again and compare the fingerprint with the EcoPulse web app.
error.fingerprint_not_confirmed: Confirm that the fingerprint matches the one in the EcoPulse web app, or cancel.

abort.invalid_discovery_info: The discovered gateway did not announce its id.
abort.unsupported_api_version: This gateway does not offer a Home Assistant API version this integration supports. Update the integration.
abort.wrong_gateway: This token belongs to a different gateway.

surplus.title: Surplus available
surplus.description: When the binary sensor "Surplus available" turns on and off, based on the gateway's solar excess power. It turns on once the excess has been at least the threshold for the whole on-delay, and off once it has been below the threshold minus the hysteresis for the whole off-delay. A missing value counts as no surplus. Changes apply immediately.

data_description.surplus_threshold_w: Solar excess power from which surplus counts as available.
data_description.surplus_hysteresis_w: Surplus only counts as gone below the threshold minus this value, so a value around the threshold does not toggle the sensor.
data_description.surplus_on_delay_s: How long the excess must stay at or above the threshold before the sensor turns on.
data_description.surplus_off_delay_s: How long the excess must stay below the threshold minus the hysteresis (or be unknown) before the sensor turns off.

inputs.title: Values from Home Assistant
inputs.description: The gateway offers {count} inputs: values Home Assistant may send to EcoPulse (for example an outdoor temperature). Pick the entity that feeds each one; leave an input empty to send nothing for it. Values are converted into the input's unit and sent on every change and every 10 seconds over the encrypted connection; an input without a value for a minute counts as missing in EcoPulse. EcoPulse's own entities are not offered.

loads.title: Loads switched by EcoPulse
loads.description: The gateway offers {count} loads EcoPulse may switch, for example a heating rod or a pool pump on solar surplus. Pick the switch, light, fan or input boolean EcoPulse switches for each; leave a load empty and EcoPulse cannot switch it. Commands arrive only over the encrypted connection. EcoPulse's own entities are not offered.

abort.no_inputs: The gateway offers no inputs. In the EcoPulse web app, add the gateway's Home Assistant driver with the devices to feed, and turn on "Values from Home Assistant" on the gateway's Home Assistant card; then reload this integration.
abort.no_loads: The gateway offers no loads. In the EcoPulse web app, add the loads on the gateway's Home Assistant card and turn on "Loads switched by EcoPulse"; then reload this integration.

inputs_refused.title: EcoPulse no longer accepts values from Home Assistant
inputs_refused.description: The gateway {name} refused the values Home Assistant sends ({code}). Either "Values from Home Assistant" was turned off on the gateway's Home Assistant card in the EcoPulse web app, or the connection is not encrypted. Reading values goes on. Turn it on again (or set up the encrypted connection), then reload this integration.

inputs_need_tls.title: Values for EcoPulse need the encrypted connection
inputs_need_tls.description: Entities are mapped to the inputs of the gateway {name}, but this integration connects without encryption, and the gateway accepts values only over its encrypted connection. Nothing is sent. Reconfigure the integration with the encrypted connection (reauthenticate and turn on TLS).

input_unit.title: A value for EcoPulse cannot be converted
input_unit.description: The entity {entity} reports its value in {unit}, which cannot be converted into {slot_unit}, the unit of the EcoPulse input "{slot}". Its value is not sent. Map an entity with a convertible unit in the integration's options.

input_loop.title: A Home Assistant input feeds EcoPulse its own value
input_loop.description: The inputs of the gateway {name} are mapped to EcoPulse entities ({entities}). EcoPulse would get its own value back, so these are not sent. Map other entities in the integration's options.

loads_refused.title: {name}: EcoPulse may no longer switch loads
loads_refused.description: The gateway refused the answer to a switch command ({code}): "Loads switched by EcoPulse" is off on the gateway's Home Assistant card in the EcoPulse web app. Switching stopped; reading goes on. Turn it on again and reload this integration.

loads_need_tls.title: {name}: loads need the encrypted connection
loads_need_tls.description: EcoPulse switches Home Assistant loads only over the gateway's encrypted connection, and this entry reads the gateway without it. Reconfigure the entry with the encrypted connection (reauthenticate) to let EcoPulse switch the mapped loads.

load_loop.title: {name}: EcoPulse entities mapped to loads
load_loop.description: EcoPulse's own entities ({entities}) cannot be loads EcoPulse switches; they are ignored. Pick other entities under Configure > Loads switched by EcoPulse.
